title: Banco Bradesco (BBD) — 21-Insider Cluster Escalation at Brazilian-Bank Turnaround Trough
summary: Bradesco's insider cluster escalated from 6 buyers / $11.27M (filed 2026-09-21) to 21 buyers / $28.95M (filed 2026-09-22) at ~R$18/share ADR-equivalent ~$3.50. A 21-insider cluster is exceptionally rare on a legacy LatAm bank and signals broad internal conviction that Q2 2026 marked the fundamental low ahead of the Selic-cut cycle.
catalyst: SEC Form 4 filings dated 2026-09-22 aggregate 21 directors and officers of Banco Bradesco S.A. purchasing common shares totaling $28.95M / 1.61M shares (openinsider composite; individual filings on SEC EDGAR). The escalation from a 6-insider cluster the day prior suggests coordinated conviction rather than one-off portfolio rebalancing. Bradesco's Q2 2026 print showed NII inflection and cost-of-risk normalization, and Brazil's Selic peaked at 15% in Q2 and is expected to begin easing into Q4 2026.
thesis: Bradesco is mid-turnaround under CEO Marcelo Noronha: re-underwriting the retail book, aggressive provisioning during Brazil's 2023-2025 rate cycle, and cost re-basing. A 21-insider cluster is empirically rare on legacy LatAm banks — the closest analog in our history is the LILA 6-insider stalk at $47M, and BBD's aggregate exceeds it in insider count. Cross-signal with our NU Holdings stalk (added 2026-09-19) gives two independent angles on the LatAm bank thaw: NU on digital-neobank expansion, BBD on legacy-bank rerating. Historically Brazilian bank equity beta to Selic-cut cycles has been ~2× (Fitch, Moody's cycle studies), and Bradesco's Forward P/E 5.5 vs. developed-market peers ~10× suggests significant multiple-expansion optionality on confirmed NII rebound.
counter_thesis: Brazilian sovereign risk is the dominant swing factor. The 21-insider cluster could reflect a defensive move by management or an internal signal that a large buyback is imminent (not necessarily conviction on external fundamentals). Selic-cut timing is not guaranteed: Q2 2026 inflation trended above the central bank's 3% target and a hawkish surprise could delay the easing cycle into 2027. Real-denominated earnings translation into USD is a persistent drag on ADR returns even if BRL is stable. Legacy-bank turnaround stories (Itau, Santander Brasil) have historically been slower to reprice than digital neobanks (NU) despite similar directional tailwinds, so cross-signal with NU may cannibalize NU's alpha. Finally, the openinsider composite value is a coarse aggregate; direct SEC Form 4 verification of P codes (open-market vs 10b5-1) is still pending.

ticker_rationale.BBD: Banco Bradesco S.A. NYSE ADR; screener IOWN 63 HOLD Dividend, Forward P/E 5.5 vs. developed-market bank peers 10x. Direct beneficiary of Selic-cut cycle through NII margin expansion on the fixed-rate loan book and through cost-of-risk normalization on the retail book. Insider cluster escalation from 6 to 21 buyers in 24 hours — without a public non-earnings news catalyst — is a strong-quality signal per the routine's criteria.

Trade construction is bounded but qualitative (entry zone is the observed insider-buy price band rather than a tight technical range; stop is at March 2026 low support). risks: Brazilian Selic-cut cycle delayed by an inflation surprise or fiscal risk repricing, extending the low-NII regime
Brazilian sovereign spread widening (5Y CDS) forcing a de-rating on all Brazilian equity ADRs regardless of company-specific fundamentals
BRL depreciation compressing USD-reported earnings even if BRL-denominated NII recovers on schedule
Q3 2026 print showing continued Brazilian retail-credit deterioration (unexpected uptick in cost-of-risk) invalidating the Q2 trough thesis
The 21-insider cluster reflecting a defensive posture (e.g., pre-buyback lockup or governance-driven mandate) rather than external-fundamental conviction

invalidation.trigger: BBD closes below $2.95 on any single day (also the stop-loss level)
Brazilian Selic policy rate raised (rather than cut) at the next Copom meeting after 2026-11-18
Q3 2026 print shows YoY NII decline or cost-of-risk expanding vs Q2 2026
Direct SEC EDGAR Form 4 verification reveals ≥50% of the 21 filings were 10b5-1 or gift/estate-planning transactions rather than open-market discretionary buys
